title: Board fits the window and grows with its Notes
lede: Before this PR, the Board was a fixed 1920×1080, so a 1024×768 window had scrollbars before a single Note existed. Now the Board is **the larger of the visible area and the Notes' extent**. CSS works that out, so it follows the window on the same frame. A Drag **measures the Board once at press** and keeps the Note inside it, so dragging never grows the Board. The Notes store no longer clamps to any far edge, so shrinking the window never rewrites a stored position (ADR 0003, superseding ADR 0001).

files.question: What decides how big the Board is?
files.summary: `min-width: 100%` and `min-height: 100%` of the scroll container, with the Notes' extent set inline as `width` and `height`. Layout takes the larger of the two.
files.owns: The rule "the visible area, or the Notes' extent if that is larger".
files.never: Needs JavaScript to follow a window resize: no `ResizeObserver`, no re-render.
files.tested: `src/board.browser.test.tsx`: no scrollbars on an empty Board at 1024×768 and 1920×1080, and the Board grows at once when the window grows.

files.question: Where does the Notes' extent come from?
files.summary: Two `useNotes` selectors return the extent's width and height as numbers and set them inline. The double-click handler measures the Board to place its Note.
files.owns: Re-rendering the Board only when the furthest right or bottom edge changes.
files.never: Reads the window size: CSS does that.
files.tested: The shrink test: with the window smaller than a Note's far corner, the Board is exactly 980×670, the Note's edges.

files.question: How are rects kept inside a Board whose size changes?
files.summary: `clampToBoard`, `toCommittedRect`, `resizeRect`, `placeCentredAt` and `placeInVisibleBoard` take the Board size as a parameter. `notesExtent` measures the Notes. `toStoredRect` is the store's window-independent rule.
files.owns: All the clamping maths, including a Board smaller than a Note (the Note keeps 140×100 at the top-left).
files.never: Holds a Board size of its own: `BOARD_SIZE` is gone.
files.tested: `src/geometry.test.ts`: every function with a 1920×1080 and a 1000×696 Board, a Board smaller than a Note, and the property tests.

files.question: How is the Board measured when a size is needed?
files.summary: `measureBoardSize` reads the rendered Board and rounds down to whole pixels.
files.owns: Turning the CSS-decided size into a whole-pixel `Size`.
files.never: Measures anything except at press or at a create.
files.tested: Through the browser tests: a move or resize at the edge stops at exactly 1000×696.

files.question: Where does a Drag get the Board size?
files.summary: The real `io.boardSize()` calls `measureBoardSize` on the Board.
files.never: Decides when to read it: the controller does.
files.tested: Excluded from coverage (DOM wiring). The browser edge tests run through it.

files.question: When is the Board size read during a Drag?
files.summary: Once, at press, into the session. Every Preview and the commit get it through `context(s)`.
files.owns: The press-time snapshot, so a window resized mid-drag doesn't change what the Drag allows.
files.never: Knows how big the Board is: it asks `io`.
files.tested: `src/drag/controller.test.ts`: a resize stops at the Board measured at press, even after the fake Board grows mid-drag.

files.question: How do move and resize use it?
files.summary: `DragContext` has a `board`. `moved` clamps with `toCommittedRect(…, board)`; a resize calls `resizeRect(…, board)`.
files.owns: Preview and commit using the same Board size, so what you release is what you saw.
files.tested: `src/drag/kinds.test.ts`, with a Board in every context.

files.question: Where does an S/M/L Note go now?
files.summary: `createInView` measures the Board at the click and passes it to `placeInVisibleBoard`.
files.owns: Placing a new Note inside the Board as it is at the click.
files.never: Grows the Board: the placement stays inside the measured size.
files.tested: `src/App.browser.test.tsx`: the per-size placement tests, and the cascade test.

files.question: Why doesn't the store clamp to the Board any more?
files.summary: Its transitions use `toStoredRect`: whole pixels, at least 140×100, no negative position, but no far edge.
files.owns: Keeping a stored position as it is, whatever the window size.
files.never: Knows the Board's size: a Drag and a create clamp before they save.
files.tested: `src/notes/notesStore.test.ts`: loading a Note at x 5000 keeps x 5000.

files.question: How do the tests prove the acceptance criteria?
files.summary: Real windows in Chromium and Firefox: empty Board sizes, Notes that fit, growing and shrinking the window, and real mouse drags at the edges.
files.never: Pushes a Note into the bottom-right corner: the Trash zone is there, so each edge is tested on its own.

scenarios.name: The window shrinks below a stored Note

steps.title: the Local copy loads a Note at (760, 500)
steps.explain: `load` passes each Note through `toStoredRect`, which rounds and keeps the Note off negative coordinates but has **no far edge**. Before this PR it clamped to 1920×1080. With a window-sized Board, a far-edge clamp here would rewrite the saved position every time the app opened in a small window.

steps.title: the Board renders with the Notes' extent
steps.explain: Each selector returns a number, so the Board re-renders only when the furthest edge moves, not on every Note change. The extent is (980, 670), the Note's right and bottom edges.

steps.title: the window goes from 1024×768 to 800×600
steps.explain: No JavaScript runs. In the large window, `min-width: 100%` (1000×696) beat the inline 980×670. In the small one, the visible area is smaller than the Note's extent, so the inline size wins, the Board is exactly 980×670, and the scroll container gets scrollbars. The test checks that the Note's stored position is still (760, 500), and that it is fully visible after scrolling to the end.

scenarios.name: Click S, M or L, or double-click, near the edge

steps.title: click on M
steps.explain: A new Note is placed inside the Board as it is now, measured at the click. Before, the cascade could run out to 1920×1080 even in a small window; now it stops at the edge of the visible Board.

steps.title: double-click on empty Board
steps.explain: The same measurement, from the Board that was double-clicked.

notes.title: CSS instead of the issue's ResizeObserver
notes.detail: The issue asked to watch the scroll container with a `ResizeObserver`. CSS `min-width`/`min-height: 100%` gives the same rule on the same frame, with no measure-then-render round trip and no fractional pixel that could add a scrollbar. JavaScript only needs the size at press or at a create, and reads it then. Counter-argument: the size isn't in a store, so a future feature that needs it reactively would have to add the observer after all.

notes.title: The visible area is the scroll container less the 24 px backdrop strip
notes.detail: The issue said "the scroll container's client size". The existing padding (`--board-end-gap`) stays, so the Board stops 24 px short on the right and bottom and the edge line stays visible. The empty hint and the Trash zone use the same strip.

notes.title: While the Board is grown by a far Note, any Note can be dragged that far
notes.detail: "Clamped to the Board's current size" means the extent when a Note sits past the window. Dragging the far Note back in shrinks the Board again. Recorded in ADR 0003.

notes.title: Nothing bounds a stored position
notes.detail: A hand-edited Local copy with a Note at x 10,000,000 makes a Board that wide: `parseNotes` checks only that numbers are finite. Not in the spec; recorded in ADR 0003.

notes.title: `placeCentredAt` also takes the Board size
notes.detail: Not listed in the issue, but `placeInVisibleBoard` and the double-click both go through it.
